result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make search a visible field on the first screen and handle typing and zero results well, including filter relaxation, spelling correction, ways forward, and offline errors. A goes further on what the app remembers: branch, session filters, saved format and audience preferences, and back-navigation state. It also details renew and hold behaviour more concretely. B's Home dashboard is a strong idea for one-tap access to status and hours, but its separate Home and Search tabs overlap, and it says less about what persists. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make search prominent, describe typing and zero-result behavior in detail, merge holds and checkouts, and remember the home branch. B goes further on the library's real tasks: it puts one-tap Renew and Renew all on My Items, includes the card barcode, and offers shortcuts like 'Renew my items' and 'Hours today' when search opens. It also says more about what carries over, such as filters kept for the session, remembered format and audience, and back navigation that keeps scroll position. A is tighter and has a clear Home screen with due-soon items, holds and hours, but it says less about renewal and the other task screens.
